title: Computable contracts for proof, validation, tests, interoperability, and optimization
question: Can one canonical contract representation support mathematical propositions, executable validation, imported schemas, module conformance, and optimizer facts without universal dependent typing or a mandatory runtime?
scope: function, type, protocol, module, service, package, and workspace scopes
inline documentation witnesses and contract attachments
proof obligations, certificates, and bounded W-owned checking
contract import, export, composition, and versioning
JSON Schema, XML Schema, WSDL, SOAP policy, and OpenAPI adapters
trust boundaries, quotas, diagnostics, and inconclusive outcomes
selectedCarriers: T<(predicate)> or a refined alias for an intrinsic value invariant
structured documentation contract: field for a declaration relation
contract-safe const fn for a reusable predicate or relation
protocol signatures plus attached relations for nominal interface requirements
benchmarkReason: WCCP0 registers a design study and makes no executable, size, latency, memory, or performance claim.

current: existing W const, protocol, documentation-test, schema, and certificate crosspoints
missing: structured documentation contract parser and resolver

sources.scope: propositions, proof irrelevance, and erasure from compiled code
compile-time computation in types, strong invariants, and complexity costs
propositions as types, proofs as terms, and theorem composition
Bend 2 laws, proof definitions, affine dependent typing, parallel execution, and reported limitations
Bend 2 law, proof, rewrite, erasure, ownership, termination, and parallel-execution semantics
Lean proof artifacts, replay, trust, and independent validation

stopCondition: Stop when parser and lowering evidence exists for each selected carrier; ContractIR identity, composition, versioning, import/export, proof obligations, certificate checking, runtime evidence, erasure, diagnostics, quotas, trust boundaries, and external-schema loss are closed; and one checked fact enables a measured optimization without changing observable semantics.
